newsitem.title: USA: Needed rain falls in dry parts of western Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Needed rain falls in dry parts of western Illinois.

text.p: Much-needed rain fell across dry corn- and soy-growing areas of western Illinois Saturday, but meteorologists said Sunday that around 40 percent of the dry area missed the rain.

"There were beneficial rains to the western half of Illinois -- about 60 percent of the dry area," said Fred Gesser, chief meteorologist at Weather Express Inc. "For the most part, I'd say 60 percent of the coverage area got 1/2 inch, and 20 to 30 percent of the coverage area got an inch."
Gesser said rainfall amounts in the coverage area varied from a few hundredths of an inch to as much as two inches.
The rain stopped Sunday morning in western Illinois, but Gesser said the area may get another dose of moisture as a cold front moves through Monday night.

"Basically what we're looking at between Monday and Wednesday is another 60 to 70 percent coverage event. The front will be moving rather slowly across the Corn Belt, slowed down by remnants of (former hurricane) Danny," Gesser said.
"One thing working in favor of corn pollination is that Danny has slowed down the front and gives us more chances for rain Monday through Wednesday," Gesser said.
The National Weather Service (NWS) said as of 0700 CDT Sunday, 0.88 inch of rain had fallen over the previous 24 hours in Springfield, Ill.
NWS weekend rainfall totals for other area cities were as follows: Peoria, Ill. 0.06; Moline, Ill. 0.37; St. Louis 1.36; Dubuque, Iowa 1.15; Burlington, Iowa 0.22.
"It wasn't exactly a flood," said Jeff Penner, meteorologist at the Weather Center. "Some areas got it and some areas didn't -- that's the way July rainfall patterns are, usually."
